title: Streamlined type adapters for Python SDK — incremental validation and streaming-friendly pydantic/dataclass interop
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: users want first-class typed models in streaming responses (both pydantic and dataclass users) but current SDK patterns either require full-message buffering before validation or provide untyped partials that are brittle for production. We need a light-weight, streaming-friendly adapter layer that can: 1) produce immediately useful typed stubs from partial chunks, 2) perform incremental/deferred validation to avoid CPU spikes during long streams, 3) interoperate with both pydantic models and dataclasses without forcing users to choose, and 4) preserve idempotency and resume semantics for retries.

Goal: ship helper APIs and internal parser that allow developers to consume an async streaming response as an async iterator of typed model instances (or partial proxies) with clear guarantees about validation, retry safety, and memory use.
acceptance_criteria: Provide SDK API: stream_as(type=ModelClass, validate='deferred'|'strict'|'none') -> AsyncIterator[ModelClass|PartialProxy]
Support pydantic.BaseModel and dataclasses.dataclass targets with same ergonomics
Add utilities: as_dataclass(obj), to_pydantic(obj) that work on partial/proxied instances
Defer full validation until either (a) the stream emits a terminal marker for the logical object or (b) the user calls .validate() on the proxy
Retry-safe resume: streams include stream_id and resume_token; SDK attaches idempotency token and can rehydrate partials on resume
Add automated tests covering large messages, chunk boundaries mid-field, invalid partial inputs, and CPU/memory profiling under heavy concurrency
Docs: publish example notebook and migration guide showing both sync and async usage
tasks: Design API surface and error semantics (PRD link below)
Implement StreamParser core with incremental JSON/YAML tolerant parsing
Implement PartialProxy with lazy validation and attribute access mapping
Hook into retry layer to persist resume_token on failures and test restore
Add pydantic & dataclass adapters and conversion helpers
Write tests (unit + integration + perf) and benchmarks
Write examples for docs and notebook demonstrating common patterns
design_notes: We prefer a conservative default: validate='deferred' to avoid CPU spikes for high-throughput streams while still allowing strict validation by opt-in.
PartialProxy will implement __getattr__ to return placeholder values when fields are missing; accessing missing required fields raises PartialFieldAccessError unless .validate() is called.
To support dataclasses we will generate a lightweight factory that fills missing fields with dataclasses.MISSING proxies and preserves type annotations for mypy support.
For pydantic models we will create a 'construct_partial' path using BaseModel.construct to avoid validation costs; full validation will reuse BaseModel.validate.

Tradeoffs: lazy validation can hide schema drift until validation time. We'll emit telemetry events when partials are returned and when deferred validation fails so teams can monitor quality regressions.

We reuse existing streaming token model: stream_id + offset + resume_token. The SDK will store resume_token in an in-memory weak map for short-lived retries and expose hooks for persistence to user code (cookie-like callback).
implementation_notes: Core parser will be a small state machine that accumulates bytes up to field boundaries (comma/brace/newline) and yields partial JSON objects when safe. This avoids buffering the entire message.

Retry integration: attach 'x-rw-stream-id' header and 'x-rw-resume-token' metadata to allow server to replay from offset. Ensure idempotency by generating client token 'rw-client-<uuid>' per top-level request.
Backpressure: expose an optional max_inflight parameter on stream_as() to limit number of in-flight partials the user can hold, preventing memory blowups.

Example usage (async):

from redwood import client
from mymodels import EventModel

async for evt in client.stream_as(type=EventModel, validate='deferred'):
    # evt may be a PartialProxy or full EventModel depending on arrival
    print(evt.id)
    if evt.is_partial:
        # call evt.validate() to force full validation when needed
        await evt.validate()

    # can also convert to dataclass: d = evt.as_dataclass()
code_examples:
# sync helper for simple consumption
with client.stream_as_sync(type=OrderModel, validate='strict') as it:
    for order in it:
        assert isinstance(order, OrderModel)
        process(order)

# more advanced: resume after transient failure
stream = client.stream_as(type=LogModel, validate='deferred')
try:
    async for record in stream:
        buffer.append(record)
except TransientError as e:
    # SDK exposes last_known_resume_token() so we can persist it and retry
    token = stream.last_known_resume_token()
    persist_resume_token(token)
    # call client.stream_as(... resume_from=token) on retry
